title: Adam's roadside recovery — remembering a benefit, then fighting to be found
summary: Adam holds roadside cover through a bundled bank benefit and remembers it only because he browsed the benefits list a fortnight earlier for something unrelated. Once he calls, the service works hard — but two of its three location methods fail, and the one that succeeds comes from his brother's phone via a company nobody in the chain owns. The service arrives on time and does what it promised; getting it to know where to come is the whole story.

actions: Holds the premium account and pays for it monthly, largely for benefits he uses occasionally
laneContent.thoughts: The account earns its keep through the things I actually claim. I couldn't list everything it includes.
laneContent.needAtStep: To be getting value from something he pays for every month

actions: Sees the full benefits list whenever he opens the app for any single benefit
laneContent.thoughts: There's more in here than I remember signing up for.
opportunities: Surface the benefit most relevant to what the customer is about to do, rather than a flat list

actions: Opens the app for half-price cinema tickets, browses the rest of the list out of curiosity, notices roadside assistance covers any vehicle he travels in across Europe
laneContent.thoughts: Roadside cover, and it follows me rather than a car. Worth remembering.
laneContent.needAtStep: To know what he is entitled to before he needs it

barriers.description: Nothing prompted this. He learned what he was covered for by accident, a fortnight before he needed it, while doing something entirely unrelated.
barriers.emergesFrom: His habit of browsing sideways in apps, colliding with a service that leaves awareness to chance

opportunities: Treat incidental browsing as the primary awareness mechanism it evidently is
Refresh awareness before known travel, using data the bank already holds

momentThatMatters.moment: Noticing the roadside cover exists and follows the person

actions: Travelling as a passenger in his brother's car when it stops and cannot continue
laneContent.thoughts: That's the day gone. Where even are we?
laneContent.needAtStep: To understand how bad this is and what happens next
laneContent.painAtStep: Stranded on an unfamiliar road abroad with family, and no immediate sense of who to call

actions: Helps get everyone safe; part of the group leaves in his father's car to continue the trip while he stays with his brother
laneContent.thoughts: Get the others moving, then sort the car. At least we're not all stuck.
laneContent.needAtStep: To make sure nobody is in danger before dealing with anything administrative

actions: Listens as his brother calls his own motor insurer and is refused for not notifying them of overseas travel
laneContent.thoughts: He bought cover for these exact dates. How is that not enough?
laneContent.painAtStep: Watching careful preparation count for nothing on a procedural technicality, with no fallback in sight

barriers.description: The obvious route refuses on a technicality. At this point they have no cover they know of and no plan, several hours from anywhere familiar.
barriers.emergesFrom: A different provider's policy condition colliding with a family who believed they had prepared properly

actions: Remembers the bank benefit, works out it should apply to his brother's car abroad, and suggests trying it
laneContent.thoughts: Hang on — mine covers any car I'm in, anywhere in Europe. That's this.
laneContent.needAtStep: To find any route to help now that the obvious one has closed
opportunities: Prompt customers to check bundled benefits at the moment another provider refuses

momentThatMatters.moment: Realising his own bank benefit might rescue the situation

actions: Opens the benefits app at the roadside and finds the roadside assistance section
laneContent.thoughts: Please load. Please still be in here.

actions: Reads the cover summary and confirms it applies to any vehicle he is travelling in, across Europe. Notes the contact options.
laneContent.thoughts: Any vehicle, UK and Europe. That's exactly our situation.
laneContent.needAtStep: To be certain the cover applies before committing to it, having just watched a refusal

barriers.description: He reads a summary written for browsing as a decision aid in an emergency, and has to work out for himself whether cover that follows a person extends to someone else's car abroad.
barriers.emergesFrom: Content designed for idle reading, encountered under time pressure at a roadside
barriers.workarounds: Read it twice to be sure

actions: Sees the app and the two phone numbers offered together, and picks the overseas number
laneContent.thoughts: Downloading an app out here will take forever. A person will be quicker.
laneContent.needAtStep: To pick the fastest route to a human who can send help
opportunities: Recommend a route based on signal and case type rather than presenting a flat choice

actions: Calls the overseas number and reaches an agent who already knows which bank's benefit applies
laneContent.thoughts: Good — they know who I am and what I'm covered for. This is going to be fine.
laneContent.needAtStep: To reach someone who can take control of the situation

actions: Is told it would be easier to use the app or the website; ends the working call and installs the app
laneContent.thoughts: They'd know best. If the app's quicker, fine.
laneContent.painAtStep: Gives up a working, answered call on the service's own advice, with no case created and nothing recorded

barriers.description: He trusts the service's recommendation and abandons the one channel that was working. Nothing is retained from the call, so the deflection costs him everything he has done so far.
barriers.emergesFrom: His deference to the service's own advice, colliding with a deflection policy that carries no state across the switch
barriers.workarounds: None — he had no way to know the app could not do the job

momentThatMatters.moment: Being told the app would be easier

actions: Downloads and opens the provider app at the roadside; finds he can raise a case without an account
laneContent.thoughts: No login needed. Sensible — someone's thought about this.

actions: Is asked for a postcode, which does not exist here, or GPS, which cannot get a fix on this signal. Neither works; the app offers nothing else.
laneContent.thoughts: A postcode? We're not even in the UK. And there's no signal for GPS. There's no other option — it just stops.
laneContent.needAtStep: To tell the service where he is, by any means it will accept
laneContent.painAtStep: The recommended channel is unusable, offers no alternative, and no route back to a person — and he has already given up the call

barriers.description: Both location methods depend on something unavailable at a European roadside on weak signal. The app has no third option and no way to hand him back to a human.
barriers.emergesFrom: His digital-first confidence colliding with an app built on home-market assumptions, in the one situation it was sold to handle
barriers.workarounds: None available in the app — he has to abandon it entirely

barriers.description: Being asked for a postcode in a country that does not use them, by an app whose selling point is overseas cover.
barriers.emergesFrom: A domestic product assumption meeting a customer using it exactly as advertised

momentThatMatters.moment: The app asking for a postcode he cannot possibly supply

actions: Calls back, navigates the menu again, waits again, and reaches a different agent with no knowledge of the earlier call
laneContent.thoughts: I was already talking to someone about this fifteen minutes ago. Now I'm starting from scratch.
laneContent.painAtStep: A second full contact for one incident, caused entirely by following the service's own advice

barriers.description: Nothing carried over. The abandoned call left no case, the app attempt left no record, and he begins again from nothing while standing at the roadside on a draining battery.
barriers.emergesFrom: His low tolerance for repeating himself, colliding with three systems that share no state

actions: Is asked first whether everyone is in a safe place
laneContent.thoughts: Right — they're asking the right thing first. That's a good sign.
laneContent.needAtStep: To feel the service has grasped that this is a roadside situation, not an admin task

actions: Confirms name, address and account details from memory, for the second time in twenty minutes
laneContent.thoughts: I gave you all this on the last call. My battery's going.
laneContent.painAtStep: Recalling account details at the roadside, on a dying phone, having already supplied them once

actions: Receives the location-capture SMS, opens the link, and watches it fail to get a fix
laneContent.thoughts: Same problem as the app. It's the signal, not the method.
laneContent.painAtStep: A third attempt at the same task, failing for the same underlying reason as the first

barriers.description: Presented as an alternative, but it needs the same position fix that already failed twice. A different channel, the same dependency, the same outcome.
barriers.emergesFrom: Weak signal defeating every method that asks the device to locate itself

actions: His brother suggests a precise-location service; Adam searches to check the provider accepts it before offering it to the agent
laneContent.thoughts: If they take this format we're sorted. Let me check before I suggest it.
laneContent.needAtStep: To find a way of describing where he is that the service will actually accept

barriers.description: He has to search the public internet, mid-call, to discover a capability the service has and never mentions. The agent did not offer it.
barriers.emergesFrom: His habit of verifying before proposing, compensating for a service that never states what it accepts
barriers.workarounds: Search engine, on the little battery left

opportunities: State plainly which location formats are accepted — in the app, on the call, and in the SMS
Have agents offer alternative formats the moment the first method fails

actions: His brother reads the location reference off his own phone; Adam repeats it to the agent, who enters it and confirms it back
laneContent.thoughts: Finally. It took three goes, my brother's phone and a company none of them work with.
laneContent.needAtStep: To be findable, so help can actually be sent

barriers.description: The thing that rescued the case was a second person with a charged phone and better signal. Alone, he would still have been stuck.
barriers.emergesFrom: A service that assumes one customer with one working device, meeting a situation where neither held
barriers.workarounds: Borrow someone else's phone and read the answer aloud

momentThatMatters.moment: The location finally transmitting, from someone else's phone

actions: Is told the case is raised, recovery will be 60 to 90 minutes, and they will be in touch if anything changes
laneContent.thoughts: An hour and a half. We can manage that. Someone's coming.
laneContent.needAtStep: To know that help is definitely coming and roughly when

actions: Waits at the roadside with his brother, watching the battery and the traffic
laneContent.thoughts: No news either way. I'll assume that means it's on track.
laneContent.painAtStep: No case reference and no way to check progress — silence could mean on track or forgotten

actions: Unaware that the case has been passed to a local recovery firm
laneContent.thoughts: Nothing to go on. I don't know who's actually coming.

actions: Receives an unexpected SMS from a local garage he has never heard of, containing a link
laneContent.thoughts: Who's this? Is this legitimate, or is it a scam? It must be them.

barriers.description: An unannounced message from an unknown company abroad with a link in it. Genuine, but with every hallmark customers are told to distrust.
barriers.emergesFrom: A handoff nobody told him about, surfacing as a cold contact from a stranger
barriers.workarounds: Assume it is legitimate because the timing fits

actions: Opens the tracking site and watches the case move to accepted, then en route with an ETA
laneContent.thoughts: That's better. I can see it happening now.
laneContent.needAtStep: To see progress rather than take it on trust
opportunities: Offer this at the point the case is raised, not an hour into the wait

actions: Takes a call from the recovery firm confirming they are on their way
laneContent.thoughts: Third message from the same people. I'd already seen it online — but it's good to hear a voice.

actions: Meets the engineer, who assesses the car and loads it
laneContent.thoughts: On time, like they said. That part worked exactly as it should.

momentThatMatters.moment: Recovery arriving within the promised window

actions: Says where they need to be taken; is told the vehicle must go to the recovery firm's own garage instead. Accepts it.
laneContent.thoughts: I'm fairly sure the cover says anywhere we need. But I'm not arguing at the roadside with the family waiting.
laneContent.painAtStep: Receives less than his cover entitles him to, with no way to check the terms or challenge it in the moment

barriers.description: He half-remembers an entitlement he cannot prove, from a summary read hours ago on a phone now nearly flat. The engineer states the opposite with confidence and does not know the cover terms either.
barriers.emergesFrom: An entitlement that lives in the bank's app colliding with a subcontractor who was sent a job, not a policy
barriers.workarounds: Comply, and raise it later if it matters

barriers.description: Challenging means delaying recovery while standing at the roadside with family. Compliance is the only sensible choice, which makes the entitlement unenforceable in practice.
barriers.emergesFrom: His pragmatism under pressure meeting an entitlement with no enforcement route

momentThatMatters.moment: Being told the car must go to their garage, not where he asked

actions: Travels roughly thirty minutes to the recovery firm's garage with his brother and the car
laneContent.thoughts: Further from where we were going, not closer. But at least the car's moving.

actions: Empties the car of what they need and completes intake paperwork, including having licences copied
laneContent.thoughts: Third time I've given these details today, and now on paper, to a company I'd never heard of this morning.
laneContent.painAtStep: The same information collected a third time, by a third organisation, on paper, in another language

barriers.description: Identity documents copied by a company two steps removed from his bank, under arrangements he cannot see and did not agree to directly.
barriers.emergesFrom: A chain of handoffs where each party collects afresh because none shares a record
barriers.workarounds: Hand them over — there is no alternative if he wants the car repaired

actions: Arranges for his father to collect them from the garage
laneContent.thoughts: We'll sort our own lift. Nobody mentioned anything about getting us onward.
laneContent.painAtStep: Onward travel and emergency accommodation were both covered and neither was offered, so neither was used

barriers.description: Entitlements he was paying for went unused because nothing surfaced them at the point they applied. He learned about them later, in passing.
barriers.emergesFrom: A cover summary read once at the start, meeting a case where the relevant entitlement arrives hours later

opportunities: Offer onward travel automatically when recovery leaves a customer somewhere they did not choose

actions: Telephones the next day for an update, because no other route exists
laneContent.thoughts: Nothing's come through overnight. I'll have to ring them again.
laneContent.painAtStep: Has to chase for news of his own case; the tracking site he was given has quietly stopped showing anything

barriers.description: Every self-service route has expired or covered only the leg that has finished. Staying informed costs him a phone call each time.
barriers.emergesFrom: His preference for asynchronous channels meeting a service that only updates on request, by phone

actions: Is told a hire car is included; says he will have to check with his brother, whose car it is
laneContent.thoughts: It's not my call. And they can't ask him — they don't even know he exists.
laneContent.painAtStep: Acting as a relay for decisions he has no authority to make, for a service that cannot contact the person who does

barriers.description: He holds the cover; his brother owns the car. Every question has to make a round trip through him, and the actual decision-maker is invisible to the service.
barriers.emergesFrom: Cover that follows a person, colliding with an asset owned by someone else

actions: Hears that his family have walked into a village garage and been pointed to another nearby that can do the repair
laneContent.thoughts: We found one in an afternoon by asking. I've no idea whether they were close to finding one themselves.

barriers.description: Nobody told him the service was already working this, or how long it might take, so duplicating the effort was entirely rational.
barriers.emergesFrom: A service that does not report its own progress, meeting a family inclined to solve things locally
barriers.workarounds: Do it themselves and tell the service afterwards

actions: Calls back with the garage details and confirms the hire car; gives occupant numbers and driver, and is offered flexible drop-off including leaving the return location open
laneContent.thoughts: They took the garage we found without any fuss, and they're happy to leave the drop-off open. That's genuinely helpful.
laneContent.needAtStep: To get the car booked in and the family mobile again
opportunities: Keep this flexibility — accepting a customer-found garage and an undecided drop-off is the best the service does

actions: Is told the hire request has been submitted to their supplier
laneContent.thoughts: Another company in the chain. I still can't talk to any of them directly.

actions: Receives an SMS with a link, opens it, and joins a messaging conversation with the provider
laneContent.thoughts: This is what I wanted from the start. Why wasn't this offered yesterday?
laneContent.needAtStep: A way to ask questions and get updates without making a phone call
laneContent.painAtStep: The lowest-effort channel in the whole service arrives after two days and three phone calls
opportunities: Offer the messaging channel at first contact, not after two days of phone calls

momentThatMatters.moment: Being handed a channel that finally costs him nothing to use

actions: Gets case updates by message from then on, without needing to call
laneContent.thoughts: Car's with a garage, everyone's safe, and I can just ask when I want to know something. We got there.
laneContent.needAtStep: To stay informed without effort while the repair runs its course

outcome.reflection: The service did what it promised: recovery arrived inside the window, the car is with a garage that can repair it, and everyone got where they were going. What took the effort was being found — two of three location methods failed, and the one that worked came from his brother's phone. He gave up a working call on the service's own advice and paid for it with a second call and a second identity check.

provenance.evidence: First-hand account given in interview while the case was still open. Emotional states and internal reasoning are the customer's own, reported directly rather than inferred.

researchSources.source: First-hand account of a live roadside breakdown case (notes held privately, outside version control)

governance.legalBasis: Not applicable — fictional composite for a published example set, derived from a consented first-hand account with name, bank, provider, country and dates removed.
